Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: 25OHD levels did not differ significantly between patients treated for depression and healthy controls.
Sentence: "The level of 25OHD and 1,25(OH)2D3 did not differ significantly between the examined groups."
Measured as: depression (patients treated for depression vs healthy controls)
Population: 99 patients aged 46.9 ± 11 years treated for depression and 45 healthy subjects
Intervention: Not applicable (observational; serum 25OHD measured)
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 144
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher serum vitamin D levels were associated with a reduced likelihood of depression compared with low vitamin D levels.
Sentence: "Logistic regression analysis indicated that individuals with higher vitamin D levels had a reduced likelihood of depression compared with those with low vitamin D levels (adjusted odds ratio (OR) = 0.950, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.920-0.982, p = 0.002)."
Measured as: depression (case vs healthy control status)
Population: 412 first-episode, drug-naïve patients with depression and 180 age-matched healthy controls
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower serum vitamin D levels
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 592
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are case-control studies of serum vitamin D and depression, but one finds no difference and the other a lower odds of depression with higher levels, and the populations differ (patients on treatment vs first-episode drug-naive).","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["design_or_bias"],"detail":"population: 99 patients aged ~47 already treated for depression vs 412 first-episode drug-naive patients; n = 144 vs 592"}
